```{python}
import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn import metrics
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuidatascience/data4dwellings/master/data-raw/dwellings_ml/dwellings_ml.csv"
df = pl.read_csv(url)

# cast before1980 to string so lets_plot treats it as a category
df_plot = df.with_columns(
    pl.col("before1980").cast(pl.Utf8).replace({"1": "Before 1980", "0": "1980 or After"}).alias("era")
)
```

## QUESTION 1

1. __Take time to get to know your data.__ Based on some initial exploration, identify 3 variables in the dataset you think will have strong predictive ability for determining if a house was built before 1980. Explain/justify the reasoning behind your guesses (for example with plots).

I looked at three variables that I thought would separate pre- and post-1980 homes pretty well: `livearea`, `stories`, and `sprice`. Older homes are generally smaller, more often one story, and cheaper. The charts back that up.

```{python}
# Chart 1: living area binned into ranges, proportion by era
livearea_counts = (
    df_plot
    .filter(pl.col("livearea") <= 4000)
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("livearea")
        .cut([1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000], labels=["<1000", "1000-1500", "1500-2000", "2000-2500", "2500-3000", ">3000"])
        .alias("livearea_bin")
    )
    .group_by(["livearea_bin", "era"])
    .agg(pl.len().alias("count"))
    .sort("livearea_bin")
)

(
    ggplot(livearea_counts, aes(x="livearea_bin", y="count", fill="era"))
    + geom_bar(stat="identity", position="fill")
    + scale_fill_manual(values=["#4393c3", "#d6604d"])
    + labs(title="Living Area by Era", x="Living Area (sq ft)", y="Proportion", fill="Era")
    + theme_light()
    + theme(legend_position="bottom")
)
```

```{python}
# Chart 2: number of stories by era
stories_counts = (
    df_plot
    .group_by(["stories", "era"])
    .agg(pl.len().alias("count"))
    .sort("stories")
    .with_columns(pl.col("stories").cast(pl.Utf8))
)

(
    ggplot(stories_counts, aes(x="stories", y="count", fill="era"))
    + geom_bar(stat="identity", position="fill")
    + scale_fill_manual(values=["#4393c3", "#d6604d"])
    + labs(title="Number of Stories by Era", x="Stories", y="Proportion", fill="Era")
    + theme_light()
    + theme(legend_position="bottom")
)
```

```{python}
# Chart 3: sale price binned into ranges, proportion by era
sprice_counts = (
    df_plot
    .filter(pl.col("sprice") <= 600000)
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("sprice")
        .cut([100000, 200000, 300000, 400000, 500000], labels=["<100k", "100-200k", "200-300k", "300-400k", "400-500k", ">500k"])
        .alias("sprice_bin")
    )
    .group_by(["sprice_bin", "era"])
    .agg(pl.len().alias("count"))
    .sort("sprice_bin")
)

(
    ggplot(sprice_counts, aes(x="sprice_bin", y="count", fill="era"))
    + geom_bar(stat="identity", position="fill")
    + scale_fill_manual(values=["#4393c3", "#d6604d"])
    + labs(title="Sale Price by Era", x="Sale Price", y="Proportion", fill="Era")
    + theme_light()
    + theme(legend_position="bottom")
)
```

## QUESTION 2

1. __Build a classification model labeling houses as being built "before 1980" or "during or after 1980".__ Your goal is to reach or exceed 90% accuracy. Report your final model choice and any other model parameters you may have tweaked (train-test split ratio, tuning parameters, etc).

I went with Random Forest since it tends to work well with the data that I selected. I dropped `parcel` since it was just an ID and `yrbuilt` since that column would literally tell the model the answer. Everything else went in as features. I used a 75/25 train-test split and 150 trees, which got me to about 93% accuracy — above the 91% target.

```{python}
features = df.drop(["parcel", "yrbuilt", "before1980"])

X = features.to_numpy()
y = df["before1980"].to_numpy()

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.25, random_state=42)

clf = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=150, random_state=42)
clf.fit(X_train, y_train)

y_pred = clf.predict(X_test)

accuracy = metrics.accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
print(f"Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f} ({accuracy*100:.2f}%)")
```
